# @cager/mcp

The Cager MCP server. It lets a coding agent push an agent to Cager, request
its release, start and control runs, and read run status and signed evidence.

Answers carry identifiers, states, counts and digests only — never output or
log text. Credentials stay in your operating system's keychain.

Requires Node.js 22 or newer.

## Install

Pick your client. Every snippet runs the server with `npx`, so there is
nothing else to install.

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user cager -- npx -y @cager/mcp
```

Or install the Cager plugin from the plugin marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add necto-technologies/necto-mcp
/plugin install cager@cager
```

### Claude Desktop

Add this to `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings → Developer → Edit Config),
then restart Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cager": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@cager/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

```sh
codex mcp add cager -- npx -y @cager/mcp
```

Or add this to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.cager]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@cager/mcp"]
```

### opencode

Add this to `opencode.json` in your project, or to
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "cager": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@cager/mcp"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

### Any other MCP client

Run `npx -y @cager/mcp` as a stdio server.

### The development platform (dev.cager.ai)

If you were invited to the development platform, add `--host push.dev.cager.ai`
after `@cager/mcp` in the snippet for your client, for example:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user cager -- npx -y @cager/mcp --host push.dev.cager.ai
```

In a JSON or TOML config, add `"--host", "push.dev.cager.ai"` to the end of `args`.
The device login then sends you to `https://dev.cager.ai/device`.

## First use

Ask your agent to sign in to Cager. It calls `cager_login`, which shows you a
one-time code and a link to the Cager console. Approve it there, signed in to
your Cager account. Pushing and running are separate approvals: the agent asks
for the push capability to push, and for run, release or read capabilities to
deploy, run and read.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cager_login` | Sign the agent in with a device code you approve in the console |
| `cager_push` | Push one source directory and its manifest, or one prebuilt image by digest |
| `cager_status` | Show the identifiers of the last push |
| `cager_deploy` | Request a release of one pushed version; a human approves it |
| `cager_run` | Start, cancel, pause or resume a run |
| `cager_runs` | Show the status of one run, or of an agent's runs |
| `cager_logs` | Show a run's lifecycle events (identifiers only) |
| `cager_evidence` | Fetch and verify a run's signed evidence |

## Configuration

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--host <host>` or `CAGER_PUSH_HOST` | `push.cager.ai` | The Cager host to talk to |
| `CAGER_EVIDENCE_KEYRING_FILE` | the ring pinned for the host | Path to the pinned evidence key ring. Without it, `cager_evidence` uses the public key ring this package pins for `push.dev.cager.ai`; for any other host it refuses to verify |

On Linux the keychain is the Secret Service (GNOME Keyring or KWallet); it
must be running.
